主要内容: The Senate Agriculture Committee passed the 2018 Farm Bill, officially known as the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018, which includes provisions for hemp legalization under federal law. This marks a significant step in U.S. agricultural policy. Senator Mitch McConnell emphasized the importance of the bill for Kentucky's agricultural economy, which includes poultry, beef, soybeans, corn, and tobacco. He highlighted the need for crop insurance and water infrastructure investments. The bill also includes funds to expand high-speed Internet and combat the opioid epidemic. The current farm bill is set to expire on September 30, and the previous version from 2014 allowed hemp cultivation for research. The Senate version would add $100 million to the dairy assistance program, on top of $1.1 billion in subsidies. SNAP benefits exceeded $63 billion in 2017, supporting over 42 million participants. The GOP-backed House bill proposed stricter work requirements for SNAP, which the White House also supports.
